note: Answers checked against jellyfin/jellyfin master at 08c2ba6 (2026-10-17). kind: documented, undocumented, decorated (doc comment above an attribute), method, rca (bug reports whose answer is the root-cause definition; checked against the branch head on 2026-10-18).

questions.q: Which middleware validates whether requests from outside the local network are allowed remote access?
Which middleware redirects requests that are missing the base URL prefix?
Which class manages installing, uninstalling and updating plugins?
Which method creates a PBKDF2 hash of a user's password?
Which class checks that the installed ffmpeg version is supported?
Which method filters a TV series' episodes down to a single season?
Which controller runs the first-time startup wizard?
Which class implements Quick Connect sign-in?
Which resolver turns movie files and folders into movie items in the library?
Which middleware turns unhandled exceptions into error responses?

One of our family accounts can't sign in from a new TV anymore. The login fails with a SecurityException "User is at their maximum number of sessions." and just before it the log shows "Current/Max sessions for user" with numbers like 2/2. We never set a limit on the account. Where is this check done, and what exactly counts as a session?

After moving our Jellyfin data and cache folders to a small SSD, the server refuses to start and dies at startup with an InvalidOperationException saying "has insufficient free space. Available:" and a Required figure of about 2 GB. The disk still has over 1 GB free. What decides this, and what is the threshold?

Users connecting from outside the house over our reverse proxy get a 'Forbidden.' error on login even with the correct password, while the same accounts work fine at home. The server log says "forbidden: remote access disabled and user not in local network". Which code rejects the login, and what conditions does it check?

Through the API, I set LoginAttemptsBeforeLockout to 0 in a user's policy, expecting that to mean 'never lock this account out'. But after 3 wrong passwords the account was disabled anyway. Why does 0 behave like 3, and which value actually turns lockout off?

I added a .ignore file to one of my movie folders so Jellyfin would skip the sample clips. Its only line was a pattern that I later found was malformed. After the next scan, the whole folder and everything under it vanished from the library instead of just the samples. Nothing appears in the logs. Why would a bad pattern hide everything?
